predicate: The reviewer complains about a delay or long wait of any kind: waiting too long for a table, food, service, a delivery, a shipment, an appointment, or a reservation (e.g. slow service, a long wait, food took 40 minutes). Answer yes if such a complaint appears anywhere in the review, even if it is not the main point; answer no if a wait is mentioned without complaint.

The review reports a hygiene or cleanliness problem at the business: dirty tables, floors, restrooms, dishes or utensils; bugs, rodents or hair in the food; or getting sick after eating there. Answer no if cleanliness is mentioned only positively or neutrally.

The reviewer praises a specific staff member, identified by name (e.g. 'Maria') or by a specific role (e.g. 'our server', 'the bartender', 'the manager'). Answer no for generic praise of 'the staff' or 'the service' as a whole.

The customer reports that the product they received was broken, damaged, defective, or stopped working (e.g. arrived cracked, died after a week, does not turn on). Answer no for complaints only about quality, size, taste, or unmet expectations when the product works.

The review explicitly says the product was a gift or present: bought as a gift for someone, or received as a gift (e.g. 'bought this as a gift for my dad', 'a Christmas present for my niece', 'I got this for my birthday'). Buying something for one's own child or household to use is NOT a gift unless the review calls it a gift or present.
